paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. On that mountain, Jesus' face changes and His clothes become radiantly white (Luke 9:29). Moses and Elijah appear in glory and talk with Him about His departure, which He was about to accomplish at Jerusalem (Luke 9:30-31). So the glory and the cross belong to the same Jesus.

Then there's Peter. He wants to put up three shelters, one for Jesus, one for Moses and one for Elijah, and the writer adds, "He did not know what he was saying" (Luke 9:33). Friend, I have been Peter, with the words out of my mouth before the thinking showed up, and I'm LOUDLY not judging him. But then a voice comes from the cloud: "This is My Son, whom I have chosen. Listen to Him!" (Luke 9:35).

That command is the whole point, baker. After the voice has spoken, only Jesus is present with them (Luke 9:36). So when you're not sure what to say or do, read what He says, let it settle in, and keep coming back for more. I think that's how a heart gets ready for the big day.
